question: Should upgrades intentionally preserve but exclude ambiguous pre-receipt subagent runs.json data from runtime state, relying on a doctor warning rather than automatically merging or deleting it?
rationale: Source inspection and proof can establish that the implementation prevents resurrection, but they cannot decide the product’s acceptable tradeoff between avoiding stale-run resurrection and automatically recovering unmatched legacy-only records from an ambiguous source.

options.title: Approve fail-closed preservation
options.body: Keep SQLite canonical, preserve ambiguous legacy files unchanged, and emit an actionable doctor warning without importing uncertain records.

options.title: Require guided recovery
options.body: Add a doctor-owned explicit resolution or recovery flow for inspecting and intentionally importing or discarding ambiguous legacy records before merge.

options.title: Pause the migration change
options.body: Do not land the runtime fallback removal until maintainers define a different compatibility contract for pre-receipt legacy state.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed preservation
recommendation.body: Keep SQLite canonical, preserve ambiguous legacy files unchanged, and emit an actionable doctor warning without importing uncertain records.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work most directly owns adjacent SQLite migration, recovery, and persisted-state safety contracts.
